Overview of ResStock building stock data for Palm Beach County Figure 5 shows the different types of residential housing units in PBC, their relative distribution, and estimated number of housing units for each different building type. For multifamily buildings, this estimated number of housing units is not the total number of buildings, but the total number of units or apartments in these types of buildings across the county. From Figure 5, we can see that while most of the households in PBC are classified as single-family, it is estimated that over 40% of housing units can be found in multi-family buildings (orange boxes in Figure 5). Figure 5: Distribution of household types in Palm Beach County To reiterate, Figure 5 does not show the number of multi-family buildings, but the number of units in these buildings. However, from the ResStock data, one characteristic of each multi-family housing unit is the number of units in that representative building. From this we can estimate the number of multifamily buildings with 2–4 units and more than five units as more than 22,000 and 13,000, respectively. In terms of unit ownership and occupancy status, Figure 6 shows that single-family attached and detached households have the highest rates of owner-occupied units in PBC, whereas more than two-thirds of multifamily units are either vacant or occupied by renters. 9 https://nrel.github.io/ResStock.github.io/docs/resources/resources.html 5 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Figure 6: Relative distribution of owners, renter, and vacant units in different building types Another important characteristic of the multi-family sector is number of units in these buildings. A multi-family building with many units and a single property manager could coordinate retrofits for a large number of housing units. Figure 7 shows that most multi-family buildings in PBC have fewer than 30 units. However, more than 17% of multi-family units are in buildings that have more than 50 units. In PBC, it is estimated that there are more than 550 of these large multi-family buildings. If targeted, these buildings could yield a significant number of very similar retrofits. There was not a meaningful difference between those who rent versus own for this dimension of the data, therefore these cohorts were not split out in Figure 7. Figure 7: Relative distribution of the number of units in multi-family buildings Figure 8 shows relative distribution of the size, in square feet, of the households separated out by building type and renter vs. owner. Across all residential building types, renters tend to live in smaller households, regardless of building type.
